list.title: Agent profiles
list.intro: An agent profile is a role in which the built-in AI works on work items: what it is told, which tools it can use, how it may write, and what it may spend. A profile only restricts; it never grants more permissions than you, the workspace, or the access already have.
list.adminOnly: Admins of this workspace can create and edit profiles.
list.loadFailed: The profiles could not be loaded.
list.emptyDescription: Without a profile, the AI works with the workspace settings. A profile like “Researcher: read-only, web allowed, $1 per work item” keeps a work item more focused.

detail.loadFailed: The profile could not be loaded.
detail.defaultHint: This profile applies to all work items in this workspace that do not specify their own.
detail.deleteDescription: {count, plural, =0 {No open work item uses this profile.} one {One open work item uses this profile and will use the default profile afterwards.} other {# open work items use this profile and will use the default profile afterwards.}} Runs keep what applied when they started. This cannot be undone.

layers.title: Profile, model, provider
layers.profile: The profile is the role: what the AI may and should do.
layers.model: The model is a preference of the profile. If it is no longer enabled, the run uses the default model.
layers.provider: The provider running the model comes from provider routing. The profile can only refine it, never bind it to a single provider.

detail.toolsAlways: Always included: navigating, searching, and reading; on a task, also reporting and asking questions; in suggestion mode, suggesting.
detail.confineNo: Runs may access all of the person’s workspaces
detail.historyEntry: {who} {action, select, created {created} updated {updated} deleted {deleted} other {updated}} the profile
detail.openWorkItems: {count, plural, one {# open task uses this profile} other {# open tasks use this profile}}

dialog.description: Each limit is compared with that of the workspace and the task; the stricter one applies.
dialog.instructionsPlaceholder: What the AI does in this role and how. For example: You find sources, substantiate every claim, and rewrite nothing.
dialog.rulesHint: The text of these pages is appended to the role.
dialog.routingHint: OpenRouter keys such as {example}, overlaid on top of the configuration. null removes a key.
dialog.routingInvalid: This is not a valid JSON object.

approval.none: The AI may complete the task
approval.review_before_done: A human completes it (AI sets “ready for review”)

workItem.label: Agent profile
workItem.help: The role in which the AI works on this work item. Subtasks inherit it. Only humans can choose this.
workItem.runsUnder: The run operates as “{name}”: with its role, tools, and limits. Without an explicit model selection, it uses the profile’s preferred model.
